text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today despite crude oil prices jumping 30% over the past two weeks—from around $96 to where it sits now. The move makes sense given the news: a reported U.S.-Russia diesel deal announced yesterday is likely dampening expectations for sustained high oil and fuel prices going forward. If the U.S. can import cheap Russian diesel to ease fuel shortages, that removes one of the biggest tailwinds that has been pushing energy stocks higher and refiner margins wider.

The broader backdrop remains volatile but less supportive than it was a few days ago. While geopolitical risks—tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, Hurricane Isaias hitting Gulf of Mexico production, and wars destroying refining capacity—have all pushed crude prices sharply higher this month, the prospect of Russian fuel flooding the market undercuts the scarcity premium that was driving the rally.
